items: **Same problem:** yeast cell counts before pitching.

**No shared employer, school or contact verified.**

lead_with.title: Complement, not replace
lead_with.text: Keep the Aber meters for in-line biomass. Amphasys adds **single-cell data** (viability, physiological state) that an average capacitance value cannot give.

lead_with.title: Check what the average hides
lead_with.text: As the team wrote: **Aber is based on capacitance and gives an average value**. A side-by-side test on a few pitches shows what extra insight he would get.

lead_with.title: Low-risk trial
lead_with.text: Propose a **small at-line comparison** on stored yeast, with no change to the current process.

history.text: LinkedIn InMail. James accepted and explained they do **cell counts off the yeast storage tanks with in-line Aber meters**, and use the same meters on the pitch; his facility is an old Miller plant. The team answered that Amphasys gives **more insight** than Aber's average capacitance value and asked for an email. James gave **jbruner@citybrwery.com** but said he is **not certain they would replace a working system**. Team: *I'll send that over and if anything sparks interest let me know.* Box created **Nov 19, 2026** by Juliana R. **Open item:** the information email.

talking_points: Who decides on yeast management and QC at your plant: brewmaster, QC lab, or maintenance?
What decisions do you take from the Aber reading today (pitch rate, yeast reuse, dumping a generation)?
Have you ever had a fermentation problem the Aber count did not explain?
Would a **side-by-side test** on a few yeast samples, without changing your process, be useful?
Do the other City Brewing plants use the same setup?
